summary: The study investigates the properties of tin oxide (SnO2) layers deposited via plasma enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) using tetrakis(dimethylamino)tin (TDMASn) and oxygen plasma. The layers were analyzed for their optical and electrical properties, and the effects of deposition temperature on these properties were examined. The results show that increasing the deposition temperature significantly reduces the resistivity of the SnO2 layers and increases the refractive index. Additionally, the study found that decreasing carbon and nitrogen contaminations in the layers leads to changes in optical band gaps and refractive indices. The presence of hydroxyl groups in the layers was also observed through XPS analysis.
evidence: Tin oxide (SnO2) layers were deposited using plasma enhanced atomic layer deposition with tetrakis(dimethylamino)tin precursor and oxygen plasma. The deposited layers were analyzed by spectral ellipsometry, conductivity measurements, and in-system photoelectron spectroscopy. Within a deposition temperature range of 90–210 /C14 C, the resistivity of the SnO2 layers decreases by 5 orders of magnitude with increasing deposition temperature. At the same time, the refractive index at 632.8 nm increases from 1.7 to 1.9. These changes in bulk layer properties are connected to results from photoelectron spectroscopy. It is found that decreasing carbon and nitrogen contaminations in the tin oxide layers lead to decreasing optical band gaps and increasing refractive index. Additionally, for the deposited SnO2 layers, a shoulder in the O 1s core level spectrum is observed that decreases with the deposition temperature and thus is proposed to be related to hydroxyl groups.
